newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian National Oil plunge shocks market.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian National Oil plunge shocks market.

text.p: Nigeria's leading petroleum products marketer, National Oil and Chemical Marketing Company, shocked the stock market on Tuesday when it announced a sharp drop in its 1996 profit, dealers said.
The result for the year ended December 31, 1996 showed an 80 percent drop in after-tax profit to 253.4 million from 1.2 billion naira a year earlier, one trader said.
There was no official explanation for the decline but company officials said several factors were responsible.

"The huge drop in profit is due to some factors including low profit margin and drop in the sale of aviation fuel because of the ban on Nigerian pilgrims to Mecca last year by Saudi Arabia," said one.
National Oil, which is the leading supplier of aviation fuel in the country, announced that turnover also fell to 14.1 billion naira from 14.6 billion naira.
"We also had big trade debts," another official said without elaborating.
Traders and analysts said they had no clue for the fall. One said he expected a bad result when it did not come on schedule but added that he was not prepared for the big decline.
"The oil marketing industry is having a hard time. It is not peculiar to National Oil," said one trader, adding that profit margins allowed marketers remained small.
Incessant appeals from the industry for the margins to be increased have so far cut no ice with Nigeria's military government which in 1994 raised pump prices four-fold.
Much of the windfall from that hike goes to the Petroleum Trust Fund, which ploughs it into restoring Nigeria's crumbling public infrastructure.
However, some traders said National Oil might also be weighed down by high overhead costs and persistent fuel scarcity which is a common feature in OPEC-member Nigeria.
Most outlets owned by marketers are usually out of business at the time of fuel scarcity while the black market booms.
National Oil is jointly owned by state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC), the local unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group and Nigerian citizens.
Nigeria's war time leader retired General Yakubu Gowon is chairman of the company's board of directors.
NNPC and Shell each has a 40 percent equity stake while the Nigerian public controls 20 percent.
National Oil said it would pay a one naira dividend as well as propose a scrip issue of one new share for six.
The share closed steady at 60.90 naira.
